criteria.dual_build_agreement: Carry out the build twice from the same changed tree, using the R-seed toolchain the first time and the candidate toolchain the second time. Promotion requires the two bundles to be byte-equal (bin/canlc and the catalogue/runtime inputs alike) and the two binaries to emit byte-equal results over the full predecessor-plus-new-feature corpus. Truth is the coincidence of the two builds rather than either build alone, so any discrepancy halts promotion. Capabilities that the seed-built binary is unable to run are omitted from the coincidence check and qualified by fixed vectors with bridge assumptions instead.
criteria.fixed_vectors: Authors working from the contracts (catalogue operation shapes, checker admission predicates, emitter target mappings) draft the expected outcome of every new binding and behavior: the can.std.test@1 operations, the http_peer operations, the test_launch sequencing and the dispatch rules. An independent reviewer signs off without consulting build output, and transcribing observed output into expectations is prohibited. The seed-built binary and candidate-built binary then replay the full set; a single byte of disagreement in either replay rejects promotion.
criteria.seed_built_oracle: Take the modified sources and build them strictly with the R-seed toolchain under its reviewed bootstrap recipe (go1.27.1 with pinned inputs). Run the new-feature corpus on the resulting seed-built bin/canlc; its output becomes the originating record for each new feature. The candidate-built binary mirrors that record byte-for-byte and contributes no originating record of its own. For any new capability outside what the seed-built binary can execute, use a fixed hand-reviewed vector and log the bootstrap shortfall as an explicit bridge assumption.
